title: Apex Failover Coordinator: connection hedging, prioritized egress shedding, and circuit leash
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem statement:
Hosted API ingress must fail over between regions without dropping live streaming sessions or violating SLOs. Current per-gateway heuristics create hard drops during regional evacuations and produce noisy telemetry. We need a coordinator ("apex" node) that makes SLO-driven regional decisions, performs connection hedging to reduce tail-loss for in-flight streams, applies prioritized egress shedding when capacity is constrained, and manages short-lived 'circuit leash' rules to prevent cascade failures.

Goals:
- Prevent >1% increase in 99th percentile streaming request completion time during controlled failovers.
- Ensure <0.05% permanent connection loss for sessions active >2s during a regional shift (target application-level resume token behavior).
- Keep total token cost overhead for hedging <8% for failover windows.
- Provide clear observability and playbook items for operators and SREs.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not implement cross-region KV cache replication; it will rely on short-lived prefix fallback and eventual background sync (separate work).

High-level approach:
- Introduce an Apex Failover Coordinator service that receives region health signals, SLO headroom metrics, and gateway telemetry and emits region-level directives: (1) hedge connections (parallel secondary routing for a bounded window), (2) egress buckets and prioritised shed lists, (3) circuit leash activation with tunable backoff windows.
- Gate directives behind SLO headroom rules: only enable hedging when a region's p99 latency is within configurable headroom and downstream capacity allows the overhead.
- Streaming-aware hedging: for streaming sessions, hedging will mirror request prefixes and KV-cache hints for a timeboxed period, attach resume tokens, and cancel lower-priority replicas on first successful completion.
- Prioritised egress shedding: classify routes by priority (critical, best-effort, low-cost) and apply proportionate shedding first against low-priority routes, preserving critical control paths and admin flows.
- Circuit leash: short-lived, per-node circuit rules to stop retry storms and to throttle rejoin attempts from a node for a bounded period to protect neighboring regions.

Success metrics / acceptance criteria:
- Controlled chaos test (see testing_plan) shows <0.05% permanent session loss and p99 increase below threshold for at least 5 failover runs.
- Dashboards exist for: regional SLO headroom, hedging overhead (additional tokens), shed rate by priority, circuit leash triggers, resumed-session ratio, and failed-resume causes.
- A playbook entry with manual override (force egress buckets, disable hedging) exists and is tested.

Design notes:
- Apex coordinator is logically centralized per-customer-region-pair, implemented as a small HA control-plane component deployed in hosted-control-plane. It only emits opaque directives; gateways enforce directives locally to avoid single-point data-plane control-plane bottlenecks.
- Directive schema (v0): {directive_id, scope, action, priority_list, hedge_window_ms, max_hedge_overhead_pct, circuit_leash_ms, reason_code, observed_metrics_signature}. (Implementation: store as protobuf on control-plane; gateways fetch diffs every 500ms.)
- Hedging semantics:
  * On directive=HEDGE start, gateway starts parallel optimistic secondary routing for new requests for hedge_window_ms. Secondary identical to primary but tagged with hedge replica id and low-cost quota.
  * On streaming sessions: gateway sends initial stream prefix and KV-cache hints to secondary; both keep shallow KV cache for hedge_window_ms to reduce cold starts.
  * First responding replica becomes authoritative; the other replica is gracefully canceled (send cancel marker to client if supported).
  * Gateways must account extra tokens to telemetry as "hedge_overhead" to reconcile billing and cost dashboards.
- Prioritised shedding:
  * Routes labelled at the API-router layer with priorities supplied by PMs and product configs.
  * Coordinator emits an ordered list of buckets to shed; gateways apply proportional shedding and use probabilistic drop with token-aware admission when available.
- Circuit leash:
  * When a gateway node repeatedly reintroduces high failure rates or causes retry floods, apex emits leash directive for the node or flow label.
  * Leash enforces exponential backoff windows for rejoin attempts and increments risk score; leash expires or is force-cleared by operators.

Telemetry and observability:
- New metrics: hedging_overhead_tokens_total, hedged_requests_count, hedged_streams_resumed_count, egress_shed_rate_by_bucket, circuit_leash_triggers, resumed_session_success_ratio, primary_failover_latency_ms.
- Dashboards: regional-failover/apex-overview, apx-hedge-cost-by-customer, failover-playbook-runbook.
- Traces: tag hedged traces with replica_id to attribute latency and success to primary/secondary.

API / Gateway changes required:
- Gateway fetch diff endpoint for directives (control-plane change).
- Hedged request lifecycle bookkeeping for billing and telemetry.
- Route priority config joiner to surface to coordinator.
- Streaming resume token handshake extension: a small wire-level marker that allows resume of canceled streams at the application boundary.

Rollout plan:
1) Canary: implement in control-plane and gateways behind feature flag; enable for internal tenants only. Run failovers to measure hedging overhead. (2 weeks)
2) Beta: enable for 10 external customers with high streaming usage, collect metrics and iterate (3 weeks).
3) Gradual rollout: tiered by region pairs, escalate to Dedicated customers after 6 weeks of stable metrics.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for directive schema and gateway enforcement logic.
- Integration tests: local multi-gateway harness that simulates region partitioning and measures resumed-session ratio.
- Chaos: repeated N-second regional drain (simulate AZ/regional outage) with hedging on/off to measure differences.
- Load test: synthetic streaming workload to validate hedging cost and egress-shed behavior under constrained capacity.
- Game-day: SRE-run with step-by-step playbook; confirm manual overrides behave as expected.

Operational playbook (short):
- Start: Activate directional drain on target region via coordinator; monitor p99 and headroom.
- If resumed_session_success_ratio drops below 98% -> rule out resume-token mismatch and increase hedge_window by 100ms.
- If hedge_overhead_tokens_total exceeds configured max -> disable hedging and enable broader proportional shedding against low-priority routes.
- Circuit leash trigger -> inspect node risk score; if false positive, manually clear leash; otherwise escalate to infra and consider node replacement.

Risks and mitigation:
- Cost spike from hedging: mitigate by strict headroom gating and per-customer max_hedge_overhead_pct. Add billing attribution and temporary cap enforcement.
- Unexpected client behavior on canceled streams: provide opt-out header and incrementally roll out; notify partner integrators.
- Control-plane lag -> stale directives could be harmful. Gateways will ignore directives older than X seconds and fall back to local safe defaults.

Open questions:
- Should hedging be allowed for very long-lived sessions (>5 minutes)? (proposal: only hedge initial reconnection windows and short-lived operations; long sessions rely on resume tokens and persistent state.)
- Exact default for max_hedge_overhead_pct per tier (P0 customers higher).

Next steps (this ticket):
- Design doc review with SRE and product (link below).
- Implement directive diff endpoint + protobuf schema (control-plane).
- Gateway hedging prototype and telemetry plumbing.
- Prepare canary jobs and dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Unit + integration tests pass; 2) Canary results: hedging overhead <8% and resumed_session_success_ratio >= 99.5% on internal tenants; 3) Dashboards populated and playbook verified in a SRE run; 4) Feature flag and manual overrides implemented.
design_notes: Apex coordinator should be treated as advisory; all enforcement lives at gateways to preserve data-plane resilience. Protobuf versioning required (v0->v1 compatibility). Lease TTL for directives should default to 15s and gateway diff interval 500ms to reduce latency to act while avoiding control-plane thundering. Circuit leash scoring uses moving-window error-rate plus retry amplification metric.
rollout_plan: Canary (internal) -> Beta (10 customers) -> Gradual (region pairs) -> GA. Feature flags at customer and region level. Monitor hedging cost and shed rates daily during rollout.
testing_plan: Unit tests, integration harness simulating region partition, chaos engineering with 10 runs, load tests for hedging cost, game-day with SRE and PM present.
risks: Cost, client compatibility, stale directives. Mitigations: headroom gates, opt-out header, directive TTLs and safe local defaults.
